title: Evaluation of Jumonji C lysine demethylase substrate preference to guide identification of in vitro substrates
protocol: Determine non-saturating enzyme concentration for JmjC KDM by conducting dilution series from the highest possible concentration to sub nanomolar levels (e.g., <1–10 nM).
Establish optimal concentration range of JmjC KDM yielding a non-saturated signal based on reaction parameters such as cofactor concentration, pH, temperature, etc.
Thaw Promega Succinate-Glo™ assay reagents on ice for approximately 1 hour before use.
For Acetoacetyl-CoA 100×, thaw specifically at 22°C–24°C for 5 minutes before addition to Succinate-GloTM Buffer.
Place a white 384-well microplate on a Peltier device and set temperature to 4°C.
Prepare 2× Reaction Buffer/Peptide Mix.
Add 2.5 μL of 2× Reaction Buffer/Peptide Mix to all experimental wells in the 384-well microplate.
Thaw JmjC KDM stock protein on ice.
Perform a 20 μl dilution series of the JmjC KDM protein in 1.5 ml Eppendorf tubes on ice using the buffer used initially for storage.
Save at least a 20 μL aliquot of storage buffer for the “no enzyme” control.
Set Peltier device to 23°C.
Add 2.5 μL of each JmjC KDM dilution to a specific microplate well containing the 2× Reaction Buffer/Peptide Mix.
Set the 384-well microplate on a plate shaker for 2 min at 22°C–25°C.
Centrifuge the plate at 240 × g for 1 min at 23°C.
For the no enzyme control (NEC), add 2.5 μL of storage buffer containing an absence of JmjC KDM protein.
Allow the demethylation reaction to occur for 60 min at 23°C.
Add 5 μL of Succinate Detection Reagent I to each assay well.
Shake the 384-well microplate for 2 min at 22°C–25°C.
Centrifuge the plate at 240 × g for 1 min at 23°C.
Incubate for 60 min at 23°C.
Add 10 μL of Succinate Detection Reagent II to each well.
Shake the 384-well microplate for 2 min at 22°C–25°C.
Centrifuge the plate at 240 × g for 1 min at 23°C.
Incubate for 10 min at 23°C.
Read the luminescence from each well using a microplate reader.
For each condition, subtract the average signal from that of the NEC average to account for background luminescence.
Visualize the data using data analysis/graphing software such as GraphPad Prism.
Determine non-saturating and linear dose-responsive JmjC KDM concentrations.
Choose a concentration of protein within the mid-linear range of relative activity.
Validate the methyl-state preference of the recombinant JmjC KDM for an established substrate.
Include an unmethylated substrate in assay validation.
Include a ‘no peptide control’ alongside the standard NEC for assay validation.
Thaw 40 μM wild-type substrate on ice.
Repeat steps using 2× Reaction Buffer without peptide substrate for NPC control.
Keep 2× Reaction Buffer on ice for same day use.
Add 1.25 μL of 40 μM wild-type peptide substrates to each experimental well containing 2× Reaction Buffer.
For the NPC, add 1.25 μL of 1× PBS to each well.
Thaw JmjC KDM stock protein on ice and dilute to 4× optimal concentration.
Prepare at least 20.63 μL of 2× JmjC KDM for all conditions with storage buffer.
Set Peltier device to 23°C (or appropriate constant temperature).
Add 1.25 μL of 4× JmjC KDM dilution to all experimental wells, except for the NEC.
Add 1.25 μL JmjC KDM storage buffer to the NEC.
Subtract the signal from that of the NPC to account for demethylation-uncoupled 2-oxoglutarate turnover.
Normalize subtracted luminescent signals to that of the peptide displaying the highest signal.
Visualize the data to represent methyl-state preference using data analysis/graphing software.
Thaw 40 μM peptide stocks for the PPS library position being tested on ice.
Make fresh 2× Reaction Buffer.
Add 1.25 μL of 4× (40 μM) peptide to experimental wells containing 2× Reaction Buffer.
For the NPC, use 1.25 μL of 1× PBS.
Thaw JmjC KDM stock on ice and dilute to 4× the optimal concentration in JmjC storage buffer.
Add 1.25 μL of 4× JmjC KDM solution to all experimental peptide conditions.
Add 1.25 μL JmjC KDM storage buffer to the NEC well.
Subtract the average signal of the NPC to account for demethylation-uncoupled 2-oxoglutarate turnover.
Normalize substrate luminescent signals to that of the wild-type peptide.
Divide the luminescent signals of reactions with experimental peptides by that of the WT peptide.
Repeat normalization steps for each mutation position.
Use PeSA software to produce a candidate KDM recognition motif based on JmjC KDM substrate preference.
Download and open PeSA software.
Select the “Permutation Array” tab at the menu.
Click “Load from File” and upload your JmjC KDM quantification matrix.
Repeat steps 23–32 using high-ranking peptides instead of PPS library peptides to validate in vitro activity of substrate predictions/rankings.
